Figure 2 | Hierarchical organisation of human cis-regulatory variation across the immune system. a, Number of discovered eQTLs. b, Hierarchical deployment of regulatory variation across multi-tissue, lineage-, cell-type-and cell-state-specific programmes, each with distinct genomic architectures. c, Properties of eSNPs across hierarchical classes: class proportions (left), distances from target-gene transcription start sites (TSS; centre) and sharing of accessible chromatin peaks across cell types (right). d, Distribution of PBMC-restricted eSNPs across biological compartments.Most are confined to lymphoid or myeloid lineages, with few shared between them. e, Enrichment or depletion (log₂ odds ratio) of promoter interactions, ChromHMM states, chromatin accessibility and activity-by-contact scores across pleiotropy classes. Black circles indicate FDR < 0.05. Broadly shared eQTLs favour promoter-associated, constitutively active elements, whereas specific variants favour distal, context-dependent chromatin. f, Illustrative directionally concordant and discordant eQTLs. g, Deviation from the expected probability of opposite allelic effects between pleiotropy levels. Discordance occurs preferentially between lymphoid and myeloid lineages and is uncommon between related cell types. h, Enrichment of discordant motif predictions among switching variants under increasingly stringent fine-mapping and chromatin-accessibility criteria. i, Regional association plots for two discordant eQTLs with opposing motif-alteration mechanisms. Effect sizes are shown for the indicated effect allele (bold) in two cell types. UMAPs show expression of relevant transcription factors and their predicted disrupted motifs, illustrating how cell-type-specific transcription-factor activity can reverse the regulatory effect of the same variant.

Figure 4 LIVI

Figure 4 LIVI factor genetics enables the investigation of gene-gene regulatory relationships.a, Overview of the approach. LIVI factor-associated SNPs (fSNPs) are colocalised with cis-eSNPs to identify regulators of multicellular programmes and define cell-type-resolved cis-trans relationships (top). Disease-specific graphs comprise edges for which both the cis-eSNP and trans-eGene colocalise independently with the same disease; mediation analysis validates these edges (bottom). b, Sankey diagram of cross-cell-type relationships supported by colocalising cis-eQTL-fQTL pairs. Nodes indicate the cis-eQTL cell type (left) and cell types contributing to the LIVI programme (right). Link width represents the number of colocalisations and colour indicates the cis cell type; only transitions supported by at least two events are shown. c, Proportion of disease loci explained by fSNPs, stratified by disease category. fSNPs explain a substantial fraction of loci, reaching a median of 30% for allergic diseases. d, Sunburst plot of colocalised cis-eQTLs and fQTLs for B-cell-related LIVI programmes. Rings show, from inside out, programme category, biological annotation, LIVI cell type, eSNP chromosome and cis-eGene. Solid white lines separate annotations and dashed yellow lines separate programmes sharing an annotation. Differences between LIVI and cis-eGene cell-type colours indicate cross-cell-type regulation. e, Asthma-specific cis-trans regulatory network. Nodes represent genes within cell types. Edge colour and shape indicate the direction of effect relative to increased cis-eGene expression, while dashed and solid lines denote cell type autonomous and non cell type autonomous relationships, respectively. Identical relationships involving multiple cell types were collapsed. f, Internal topology of an IRF8-associated LIVI factor comprising 17 genes. IRF8 interacts directly with a single programme member, which regulates the remaining genes through downstream interactions. g, Crohn's disease regulatory relationships converging on IL6ST. SEC16A expression in pDCs is protective by reducing JAK2 and IL6ST expression through ATP5F1E, whereas WBP4 increases risk by inhibiting ATP5F1E, thereby increasing IL6ST expression (left). Single-cell estimates identify the cell types mediating each cis-trans relationship (right). Solid lines represent the inferred graph while dashed lines represent the observed MR effect estimated through cis-eQTL colocalisations.

Human genetics guides therapeutic intervention through cell-type-resolved regulatory maps. a, Analytical framework integrating fine-mapped single-cell eQTLs and GWAS associations to prioritise disease genes, infer therapeutic direction and identify repurposing opportunities and potential adverse effects. b, Concordance between genetically inferred therapeutic direction and approved drug mechanisms. Associations are shown before stratification by therapeutic direction. e, Examples of genetically supported repurposing and adverse effects.
